correctness.rationale: Product characters diagonalize the kernel, with level-k eigenvalues obtained by expanding nonzero differences. For k<n, the g_{k,a} alternating sums have decreasing positive magnitudes uniformly q≤1/n+1/n^3; every such eigenvalue stays strictly positive. The top eigenvalue F_n(q)=sum (-1)^j C(n,j)q^{j^2} has F_n(1/n)>0, F_n(1/n+1/n^3)<0 and is strictly decreasing in the bracket via explicit binomial tail bounds. The only crossing has multiplicity (r-1)^n. Asymptotic inversion of 1-nq+C(n,2)q^4+O(n^-6) gives coefficients 1/2,-1/2,1,-2. Independent exact tests for n=2..13, r=2,3,6 and independent symbolic expansion agree; not an exhaustive infinite-dimensional computation.
